what: MiniPlay live-board saturation search beyond 40 new games a second, two fixes (a per-board live broadcaster and a pooled gateway upstream transport), and A/B checks
dates: steps, profiles and the first two A/Bs on 2026-10-22 (evening, SGT); a repeat A/B of base against the final code on 2026-10-23 (morning)
hardware: Apple M3 Pro (11 cores), 18 GiB memory, macOS 15.3.1; services and the probe ran natively, Redis and Kafka in Docker Desktop 29.5.3 (its VM and port-forwarding backend are on the same machine)
shared_machine_note: Other projects' agents shared the laptop; host load averages are recorded per run. Every measured run held the workspace's shared CPU lock.

versions.postgresql: 18.6 (Homebrew binaries), a new disposable cluster per run on 127.0.0.1:55432, TCP only, max_connections=200
versions.redis: redis:7.4-alpine (7.4.11), new container per run on 127.0.0.1:16379
versions.kafka: apache/kafka:3.9.1 single-node KRaft, new container per run on 127.0.0.1:19092, topics score.events and score.deadletter with 3 partitions

variants.base: the previous version (each live socket has its own Redis subscription and rebuilds its own frame; gateway proxies use http.DefaultTransport)
variants.broadcaster: base plus internal/httpapi/broadcast.go, the live.go and leaderboards.go changes, and store.Redis.Ranks; the gateway binary is byte-identical to base
variants.broadcaster+gateway_pool: broadcaster plus cmd/gateway upstreamTransport (MaxIdleConnsPerHost 256); every other binary is byte-identical to broadcaster
variants.note: load-probe was the same binary in every run (it adds a start_lag measurement to the committed probe)

stack: migrate, session-svc :18081, score-svc :18082, leaderboard-svc :18083, gateway :18080 serving web/dist, outbox-publisher and stats-worker; a new per-run HMAC secret from openssl rand that was never written down

probe.per_run: open the player's live socket on the all-time Pulse Field board, POST /api/sessions, wait 10.2 s, POST /api/scores with 12 replayed hits, time from submission to the first frame carrying the player's rank (frame timeout 15 s, HTTP client timeout 10 s)
probe.clients: each run has its own user and its own synthetic address from 198.18.0.0/15 in X-Forwarded-For
probe.start_lag: how late each scheduled start was; p99 stayed at or under about 10 ms in every run, so the probe kept its schedule

measurement.cpu: process_cpu_pct avg is cumulative CPU time over the probe's lifetime divided by wall time; peak_2s is the largest 2-second interval. 100% is one core of 11.
measurement.docker: docker_desktop_backend is com.docker.backend (it forwards published ports into the VM); docker_vm is the Virtualization.framework process running Redis and Kafka
measurement.redis: CONFIG RESETSTAT before the probe; commandstats after (Lua-internal calls are counted too); INFO clients 40 s into the probe; SLOWLOG threshold 1 ms (the log holds at most 128 entries)
measurement.tcp: netstat 40 s into the probe, counted by the service port at either end; macOS ephemeral ports are 49152-65535 (16,384) and TIME_WAIT lasts 30 s
measurement.sql: after the outbox drained: run_attempts, scores, rejections, outbox rows, unpublished, processed events and the daily accepted sum

findings.base_saturation: Rank-frame latency rose sharply between 40 and 80 new games a second (p50 42 -> 143 ms) with no errors; from 120 a second requests failed with 'connect: can't assign requested address'.
findings.base_cause: Every live socket rebuilt its own frame after every change (three Redis round trips per socket per change) and held its own Redis subscription, all through Docker Desktop's port forwarding; Redis throughput fell as load rose. Each socket also cost three loopback connections, and closed connections hold ports for 30 s.
findings.fix_1_broadcaster: One hub per board per process: one subscription, one completeness check and top-20 read and one pipelined rank lookup per change; slow sockets keep only the newest frame.
findings.fix_2_gateway_pool: The gateway's reverse proxies used http.DefaultTransport (2 idle connections per host), so most proxied requests opened and discarded a connection; a shared transport keeps 256 per service.
findings.after_fixes: Every game accepted through 160 new games a second (about 1,700 player sockets plus 50 watchers), rank-frame p99 172-204 ms. From 200 a second the one-host test runs out of ephemeral ports (each game holds two loopback connections plus 30 s TIME_WAIT) while measured processes use about 3.5 of 11 cores.
findings.next_code_limit: Each board's hub builds frames serially and a build grows with watching players; changes per watcher frame rose from about 1 at 40 a second to 5.5 at 160.

smoke_run_not_reported: a short 8-second run at 5 a second checked the scripts before the profile (40 games, all accepted)

broadcaster_ab_80_per_s_2026_10_22.order: base, broadcaster, base, broadcaster; each on a fresh stack

profiles_80_per_s_2026_10_22.how: separate runs with a pprof listener compiled into leaderboard-svc only (a temporary file, not committed); 15 s CPU profile from 22 s into the probe; goroutine count at 22 s
profiles_80_per_s_2026_10_22.base_cpu_profile: about 160% CPU; 44% of samples under go-redis connection reads, 27% under the per-socket completeBoard, 7% writing WebSocket frames
profiles_80_per_s_2026_10_22.broadcaster_cpu_profile: about 94% CPU; 77% writing WebSocket frames, 3% building boards (completeBoardRanks), Redis about 2%

gateway_ab_160_per_s_2026_10_22.order: broadcaster, +gateway pool, broadcaster, +gateway pool; each on a fresh stack

final_ab_80_per_s_2026_10_23.order: base, broadcaster+gateway_pool, base, broadcaster+gateway_pool; each on a fresh stack with its own lock hold; binaries rebuilt from a temporary worktree at the previous version and from the final tree, byte-identical to the 22 October builds
final_ab_80_per_s_2026_10_23.conditions: the laptop was on battery (29% falling to 25%) with Low Power Mode on; each run was wrapped in caffeinate -i to stop idle sleep

discarded_ab_2026_10_23: An earlier set at 80 a second the same morning (08:42-08:58) is not used. Its fourth run (broadcaster+gateway_pool) was disturbed: the laptop, on battery with a 1-minute idle-sleep setting, went to sleep mid-run and woke at 08:57:28, so 201 score requests arrived after their 120-second run tokens expired (401) and the probe's background sockets hung until wake. Its first three runs were normal (rank-frame p99 428 and 523 ms for base, 87 ms for the fix), but an A/B with one invalid run was discarded whole and rerun under caffeinate.
opt_in_redis_tests_2026_10_22: TestRedisBoardRecoveryIntegration, TestRedisBoardPublishesOnlyChangesIntegration and the new TestRedisRanksIntegration passed against a disposable redis:7.4-alpine (7.4.11) DB 15; the DB was empty afterwards

unit_tests.gateway_connection_reuse: 3 rounds of 16 concurrent requests through the proxy: http.DefaultTransport opened 44 upstream connections, upstreamTransport 16 (repeated 3 times)
unit_tests.broadcaster: one Redis subscription and one board read per change for two sockets on one board; subscription closed with the last socket and reopened for the next; a slow socket keeps only the newest frame; the shared frame matches the old JSON exactly; ranks fall back to SQL without reading an unverified Redis board

limits: One laptop, synthetic players, everything on loopback; not a capacity claim for any deployment.
Redis and Kafka ran behind Docker Desktop's port forwarding, which cost more CPU than Redis itself in the base runs.
The probe opens one socket per game from one host, so its own connections share the host's 16,384 ephemeral ports with the services' connections.
Steps are single runs; each A/B has two runs per variant.
